errors.text_span: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of problem difficulty levels across four categories: easy, medium, hard, and N+K-.
errors.evidence: The figure contains three separate pie charts, not a single one. The description incorrectly interprets the entire figure as one chart and confuses the titles of the three charts ('easy', 'medium', 'hard') for slice categories.

errors.text_span: The “easy” slice is green and occupies approximately 45.9%, the “medium” slice is orange and represents roughly 44.6%, the “hard” slice is teal and accounts for approximately 36.8%, and the “N+K-” slice is yellow and represents approximately 7.0%.
errors.evidence: This sentence incorrectly assigns attributes to hallucinated slices. For example, it states the 'easy' slice is green and 45.9%. 'easy' is a chart title, not a slice. In the 'easy' chart, the green (teal) slice is 40.6% and the 45.9% slice is yellow. Every mapping in this sentence is incorrect.

The description fails to state the actual purpose of the figure, which is to compare the distribution of four categories ('N+K+', 'N-K+', 'N-K-', 'N+K-') across three different conditions ('easy', 'medium', 'hard').
The description incorrectly states that a legend is not included, when one is clearly visible on the right side of the figure.
